memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made a horn at each of the four corners, so that the horns and the altar were of one piece, and they overlaid the altar with bronze." - Exod 38:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four horns, one at each corner, not attached but formed as part of the altar itself.

Those horns mattered enormously in Israel's life. Blood was put on them at the great sacrifices (Lev 4:7). And in moments of desperate danger, people ran to the altar and grabbed hold of the horns, seeking refuge — Adonijah did exactly that when he feared for his life (1 Kgs 1:50).

So the horns became a picture of taking hold of God's provision when you have nowhere else to run.

Notice they were "of one piece" with the altar. The place of refuge and the place of sacrifice were not two different things. You could not grab safety without touching the altar where blood was shed.

That is precisely our situation. Our refuge is not separate from the cross; it is the cross. Hebrews speaks of those who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us, an anchor for the soul (Heb 6:18-19).

Note also the bronze. Not gold here — bronze, which withstands fire. This altar was built for burning, and God specified a metal that could take it.

If you are running today, run here. The horns are still within reach.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you run when you are afraid?
2. Have you truly taken hold of Christ, or only admired Him from a distance?
3. What are you trying to find refuge in that cannot bear the weight?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I take hold of Christ as my only refuge. Thank You that there is a place to run. Amen.
